newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGB futures end sharply higher on short-covering.
newsitem.headline: JGB futures end sharply higher on short-covering.

text.p: Key June Japanese government bond (JGB) futures ended Tuesday's Tokyo session sharply higher as dealers covered their short positions in the late afternoon.
The benchmark contract closed up 0.76 at 124.15, after trading between 123.12 and 124.17. Turnover was 65,190 lots.
"After seeing investors buy cash JGBs, dealers decided it may be a good idea to cover short positions set up below 124.00," said a brokerage house trader.
Investors, including some medium-sized life insurers, were buying at the long-end of the yield curve, particularly the 190th to 194th JGBs, traders said.
Traders also said there was talk that public fund bodies bought cash JGBs with three to five years remaining until maturity.

Short-covering in the June futures contract was increasing ahead of the expected roll forward of the benchmark futures contract, traders said. June expires on June 9. "Turnover in September futures exceeded one trillion yen today. There seem to be moves to cover June and short September," said the brokerage house trader.
Turnover in the September contract was 10,083 lots, up from 6,019 lots on Monday.
Traders said a late afternoon fall in Tokyo stocks also contributed to the JGBs' strength.
The Nikkei 225 stock average ended down 14.40 points, or 0.07 percent, at 20,129.11, after rising as high as 20,452.35.
A bigger-than-expected decline in Japan's machinery orders for March also invited some buying in the mid-afternoon, traders said.

Japan's private-sector machinery orders, excluding those for electric power companies and for ships, fell a seasonally adjusted 12.7 percent month-on-month. The consensus forecast indicated a fall of about nine percent.

"The Economic Planning Agency's forecast for machinery orders in the April-June quarter is a rise of 4.5 percent quarter-to-quarter. However, people ignored this and chose instead to focus on the March figure," said a trader at a trust bank's securities unit.
Traders said Industrial Bank of Japan's (IBJ) new 2.2 percent five-year bank debentures attracted buying by city banks and non-life insurance companies.
IBJ said on Monday it would raise the coupon rate of its May five-year debenture by 0.6 point to 2.2 percent from 1.6 percent for the April issue.
Investors were drawn to IBJ debentures due to a higher coupon rate, traders said. In inter-dealer trade, IBJ's May debentures were traded above par in the afternoon, traders said.
The yield of the benchmark cash 182nd JGB stood at 2.505 percent as of 4.30 p.m. (0730 GMT), down sharply from Monday's close of 2.590 percent.
